question: In simple terms, what does 'demand' mean when we talk about health services?

options.A: The total amount of care that patients want and can use
options.B: The cost of buying medical equipment from abroad
options.C: The total number of doctors in a government hospital
options.D: The maximum number of beds a health center can hold

explanation: You've got this! Demand simply means the healthcare services people need and are able to access. Think of it as the care patients are asking for and using. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is asking for healthcare different from buying regular everyday goods like shoes or food?

options.A: Patients can easily diagnose and prescribe their own meds
options.B: Healthcare services are always completely free from the government
options.C: Sickness usually happens without warning and patients need professional guidance
options.D: The supply of doctors and nurses is totally unlimited everywhere

explanation: Spot on! You can't really plan when you'll fall ill. Because medical needs come suddenly, patients rely heavily on expert advice rather than just shopping around casually. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which group of people usually needs to visit the hospital or clinic the most?
explanation: Great thinking! The very young and our elderly grandparents have bodies that are more delicate against infections, so they tend to need healthcare services more frequently. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h2)

question: How does low health awareness usually affect when people go to the hospital?

options.A: It often delays people from seeking care until their sickness gets really bad
options.B: It makes them rush in immediately for minor surgeries
options.C: It forces patients to only use expensive private hospitals
options.D: It stops communities from needing health education entirely

explanation: Exactly. When people don't recognize early signs of illness, they often stay at home or use local herbs, only visiting the clinic when things turn into an emergency. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the most important human resource needed to keep a healthcare system running?
explanation: Too easy! Skilled clinical staff like nurses and doctors are the heartbeat of any hospital; without them, patient care just cannot happen. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h3)

question: A rural health post keeps running out of basic drugs and has no steady electricity. Which part of health economics is this?

options.A: The age distribution of the community
options.C: The cultural beliefs of the patients

explanation: You nailed it! Things like drugs, equipment, and steady power are vital parts of healthcare *supply*. When they are missing, the clinic's ability to provide care drops. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is a major problem with making patients pay cash directly out-of-pocket every time they visit the hospital?

options.A: Hospitals automatically get too much money from foreign donors
options.B: Diseases completely vanish from poor communities
options.C: Patients often delay or avoid getting care because they don't have immediate cash
options.D: The number of nurses in the village instantly doubles

explanation: Spot on. Paying cash right at the counter is a huge barrier for many families, forcing them to stay home and suffer rather than seek help. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does health insurance make it easier for people to get medical care?

options.A: By making all drugs and lab tests completely free to manufacture
options.B: By making it so hospitals no longer need to hire nurses
options.C: By pooling money together so the cost is shared across a large group of people
options.D: By ensuring that no one with insurance will ever catch a chronic illness

explanation: Brilliant! Insurance works like a cooperative contribution—everyone chips in a little so that when someone falls sick, the heavy bill is easily paid from the shared pool. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h4)

question: In healthcare, what do we mean by 'information asymmetry'?

options.A: Pharmacies hide drug prices from the public
options.B: Government agencies control all hospital budgets
options.C: Patients and doctors share the exact same level of medical knowledge
options.D: Healthcare providers have deep medical training while patients know very little

explanation: You got it! It simply describes the knowledge gap: doctors and nurses spent years studying medicine, while patients usually rely on them to explain what is wrong. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal market problem (imperfection) in healthcare?

options.A: Adverse selection where mostly sick people join insurance plans
options.B: Patients having perfect, expert knowledge of all complex medical treatments
options.C: Information asymmetry between the doctor and the patient
options.D: Moral hazard linked to having full health insurance

explanation: Well done! Patients definitely do *not* have perfect medical knowledge. The reality that patients lack this insider knowledge is actually a major market imperfection! [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is it helpful for a ward nurse manager to understand patient demand trends?

options.A: To stop patients from ever needing admission records
options.B: To schedule staff properly and ensure coverage during heavy illness seasons
options.C: To step in and perform complex surgeries alone in the theatre
options.D: To set market prices for private pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Exactly right! Knowing when patient numbers are likely to spike (like during malaria or harmattan seasons) helps nurse managers plan shift rosters so the ward isn't short-staffed. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h6)

question: A nurse manager notices that gloves and syringes are being wasted carelessly on the ward. What nursing responsibility does this touch on?
explanation: You're doing great! Resource stewardship simply means taking good care of hospital supplies so there's always enough equipment left to treat patients safely without wasteful spending. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h6)
